title: Let the environment swallow the completed phrase

motion.summary: DISAPPEARED BELOW appears above a turbulent sea; the phrase descends into the foreground waves and is absent in the last sampled frame.
phases: Build and hold a high-contrast two-line phrase.
Lower the phrase while foreground water overlaps it, ending on the environment alone.
motion.transferablePrinciple: A narrative force should cause the text exit, so the disappearance itself completes the meaning.
variations: Let fog, falling ash, growing foliage, sand or crowd silhouettes consume a phrase.
A recovery scene can uncover text from behind a foreground layer.
Use solid paper or fabric layers for a stylized version of the same depth relationship.
cautions: Keep the phrase readable before the masking starts.
The occluder needs a credible foreground edge rather than a rectangular wipe.
Build a fresh environment for each new scene.

quality.reviewer: agent visual inspection of decoded frame sequence
strengths: The final absence has a clear cause visible in the composition.
Foreground overlap makes the phrase belong to the scene depth.
limitations: Stills establish the stages but do not independently judge the exact easing or musical alignment.
The source sea combines imagery with added motion; this is not evidence of a fully simulated fluid scene.
Observed from six decoded frames of the exact hashed MP4; this is a concept reference, not full motion, audio-sync or whole-film acceptance.
